title: Levioso: Efficient Compiler-Informed Secure Speculation
problem: Spectre-type attacks exploit speculative execution to leak secrets through multiple transmission channels. Existing hardware-only defenses lack program knowledge and conservatively restrict all potentially-leaking instructions, incurring substantial performance overhead.
motivation: Modern CPU performance depends on speculative execution, but this feature enables exploitable side-channel vulnerabilities that leak sensitive information.
method: Levioso combines compiler analysis with hardware defenses: the compiler identifies which instructions can potentially leak secrets and exposes this program knowledge to hardware. The hardware then uses this compiler-derived insight to selectively restrict speculative execution only where necessary, rather than applying conservative blanket restrictions. This targets both speculative and non-speculative secret leaks through compiler-hardware cooperation.
key_novelty: Using compiler-identified leak points to guide selective hardware speculation restrictions, achieving security without the performance penalty of conservative hardware-only defenses.
contributions: Compiler analysis to identify instruction-level leak points
Selective speculation restrictions guided by program knowledge
Efficient defense against both speculative and non-speculative information leaks
